title: IN TROUBLE AND OUT OF OPTIONS

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The Israelite overseers realised they were in trouble when they were told, "You are not to reduce the number of bricks required of you for each day." When they left Pharaoh, they found Moses and Aaron waiting to meet them, and they said, "May the Lord look on you and judge you! You have made us obnoxious to Pharaoh and his officials and have put a sword in their hand to kill us."" - Exodus 5:19-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The overseers walk out of the palace with nothing, and the first people they see are Moses and Aaron. All their anger lands there.

Their words are bitter: may the Lord look on you and judge you. Days earlier these same people had bowed and worshipped when they heard God had seen their misery. Now they want the messengers judged.

Suffering does that. It makes us turn on the nearest available person, often the one trying to help.

Two things are worth taking from this. First, if you are serving God and people have turned on you, you are in good company — Moses, the prophets, and Christ Himself all experienced it. Do not measure your obedience by the gratitude you receive.

Second, if you are the one lashing out, be honest before God about it. He can handle your anger. But be careful not to wound the people He sent to help you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I blamed someone for a hardship that was never their fault?
2. Am I willing to keep serving even when I am misunderstood?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, guard my tongue when I am hurting. Help me not to wound those You have sent to help me, and to keep serving when I am blamed. Amen.
